newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore to shorten share settlement period.
newsitem.headline: Singapore to shorten share settlement period.

text.p: Singapore will shorten the time within which investors and stockbrokers must settle their share transactions, Finance Minister Richard Hu said on Tuesday.

Hu said the Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES) would introduce a Delivery Versus Payment (DVP) system in the first quarter of 1997 which would cut the settlement period after a share trade to just three days from the current five days.
He said the new system would improve the SES's clearing and settlement system to reduce settlement risks and transaction costs.

"Cash flows of both investors and SES member companies will improve, and they will no longer need to finance their holdings of securities transacted," Hu told an audience at the launch of Singapore's new regional share index.

In another move aimed at boosting liquidity in local shares, Hu said the SES would launch a formal securities borrowing and lending facility, via its computer terminals, where information on the demand and supply for securities lending and borrowing was publicly disseminated.
"The new facility will allow fund managers to manage and hedge their investment portfolios more actively and efficiently," Hu said.
